skill.name: smtp-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized SMTP security assessments, including service discovery, user enumeration checks, relay testing, authentication testing, and mail security hardening.
skill.summary: Assess SMTP servers for relay, enumeration, authentication, TLS, and email authentication weaknesses.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: I confirmed critical and high-risk findings for Metasploit usage, Nmap scanning, SMTP user enumeration, relay testing, credential brute force, and spoofing workflows. Some Markdown backtick and private IP detections are false positives, but the skill still contains direct operational attack guidance. Legal and ethical cautions are present, but they do not neutralize the misuse risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit, Hydra, and Medusa instructions, or limit them to an isolated lab with non-real accounts and explicit safety gates.
Delete phishing preparation language, spoofed executive messages, hidden Bcc examples, and malicious-header examples.
Replace live relay exploitation steps with defensive validation guidance that uses controlled recipients and does not send third-party mail.
Add strict scope checks, rate limits, allowlisted targets, and stop conditions before any service discovery or enumeration step.
Require the user to provide written authorization, target ownership, and testing window before giving operational steps.

content.value_statement: Mail servers can expose users, relays, weak credentials, and missing authentication controls. This skill organizes authorized SMTP testing and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Maps SMTP services, ports, banners, and supported protocol extensions.
Checks user enumeration exposure through VRFY, EXPN, and RCPT behaviors.
Tests whether a server accepts unauthorized relay attempts.
Assesses weak SMTP authentication using common security testing tools.
Reviews STARTTLS, cipher exposure, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records.
limitations: Requires explicit written authorization and a defined target scope.
Includes offensive tooling that can disrupt or abuse production mail systems.
Does not verify that the requester owns the target infrastructure.
Some results depend on wordlists, rate limits, and server response behavior.

use_cases.title: Audit mail server exposure
use_cases.description: Review SMTP ports, banners, relay behavior, and authentication controls during an authorized assessment.

use_cases.title: Harden enterprise email infrastructure
use_cases.description: Translate SMTP test results into clear remediation steps for relays, enumeration, TLS, and authentication records.

use_cases.title: Prepare a lab security exercise
use_cases.description: Create a controlled SMTP testing plan for training without using real users or production mail servers.

prompt_templates.title: Review basic SMTP scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authorized SMTP assessment scope for [domain]. Identify safe discovery steps and the evidence I should collect.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret banner findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these SMTP banners and response codes, summarize likely risks, false positives, and administrator follow-up questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan relay and enumeration checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bounded test plan for relay exposure and user enumeration on approved mail servers. Include stop conditions and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Write remediation report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these authorized SMTP findings into an executive summary, technical impact, prioritized fixes, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Authorized notes show VRFY enabled, EXPN disabled, and STARTTLS available on the submission port.
output: Finding: User enumeration is possible through VRFY responses.
Impact: Attackers can validate mailboxes before phishing or password attacks.
Fix: Disable VRFY or return uniform responses for unknown users.

output_examples.input: Relay testing accepted an external recipient from an unauthenticated connection.
output: Finding: The server appears to permit unauthorized relay.
Impact: The service may be abused for spam or impersonation.
Fix: Require authentication or restrict relay by trusted networks only.

output_examples.input: DNS review finds SPF soft fail, no DMARC policy, and missing DKIM evidence.
output: Impact: Spoofed messages may be harder for recipients to reject.
Fix: Publish aligned SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records with monitoring.

best_practices: Test only systems you own or have written permission to assess.
Use lab targets for brute force, spoofing, and relay exercises.
Record evidence, stop conditions, and remediation owners before testing.
anti_patterns: Do not use enumeration results to prepare phishing or spam campaigns.
Do not brute force production accounts without explicit approval and safeguards.
Do not send live relay traffic to third-party recipients.

faq.question: Does this skill require authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. SMTP testing can affect real services and users, so written authorization is required.

faq.question: Can it test open relay exposure?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes relay checks, but those checks should use controlled recipients and approved systems.

faq.question: Does it include brute force guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It references authentication testing tools, which create high risk outside controlled assessments.

faq.question: Can it help with defensive hardening?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers disabling enumeration, enforcing TLS, adding rate limits, and improving SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

faq.question: Does it run tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is instructional text, but it provides commands that a user could run separately.

faq.question: Is it suitable for public marketplace publishing?
faq.answer: It needs strong review because it includes offensive workflows, exploit framework usage, and credential attack examples.
